title: Quasi-affine locus of the affinization with affine generic fibre
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], with fraction field $F=\operatorname{Frac}R$ (localization at its nonzero elements) and residue field $k=R/\mathfrak m_R$, and put $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $Y\to T$ be smooth, separated and of finite type [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; separated means its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Assume its generic fibre $Y_F$ is affine [def-pc-base-change]. Put $A=\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$, and let $a:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be the canonical $T$-morphism corresponding to $\mathrm{id}_A$ under [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme]. This morphism is separated and of finite type. Let $W\subseteq Y$ be its quasi-finite locus: the points at which $a$ is quasi-finite in the sense of [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Then $W$ is a quasi-compact open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion], $W_F=Y_F$, and $a|_W$ is an open immersion. In particular $W$ is quasi-affine, meaning a quasi-compact open subscheme of an affine scheme [def-nagata-quasi-affine-morphism]. If $Y_k\ne\varnothing$, then $W_k\ne\varnothing$. No claim that $W_k$ meets every component is imposed, and no group law or descent datum is assumed. The conclusions include $Y=\varnothing$ and empty special fibre.

source.place: BLR 6.5 Lemma 6, printed p.161 (PDF p.167), and the proof of Theorem 1, printed p.162 (PDF p.168), assertions (i) and (iii) for the quasi-finite locus of the canonical affinization; the latter uses Zariski Main Theorem 2.3/2-prime. Local PDF WANTED; primary scan read online.

proof.text: Choose a uniformizer $\pi$ of $R$. A DVR is a PID, so $R$ is a Noetherian integrally closed domain of dimension one. Its prime localizations are normal, hence $T$ is normal. The finite-type-over-Noetherian lemma makes $Y$ Noetherian; separatedness over the affine $T$ makes $Y$ separated as a scheme. Every open of the Noetherian scheme $Y$ is quasi-compact by the Noetherian-open lemma. In particular intersections of affine opens are quasi-compact, so $Y$ is quasi-separated; it is also quasi-compact. These facts also show that the canonical map $a$ is quasi-compact: its source is quasi-compact and its affine target is quasi-separated.

Choose a finite affine cover $V_j=\operatorname{Spec}C_j$ of $Y$ with each $C_j$ finitely generated over $R$, as in the finite-type definition. On each such chart write $C=C_j$. The same finite list of algebra generators generates $C$ over $A$, since $R\to C$ factors through the section map $A\to C$. Thus $a$ is locally of finite type, and its quasi-compactness in step 1 makes it finite type. The composite $Y\xrightarrow a\operatorname{Spec}A\to T$ is the original separated morphism; separated cancellation gives separatedness of $a$.

source.place: Finite-type definition on affine charts; Schemes Tag 01KV.

proof.text: Apply relative normalization to $a$, writing $Y\xrightarrow i C\xrightarrow n\operatorname{Spec}A$. In its affine-chart clause (iii), take the entire target. The algebra map $A\to\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)=A$ is the identity by the definition of $a$. Its integral closure inside $A$ is exactly $A$: each element satisfies its monic linear polynomial. Consequently $C$ is affine and $n$ induces the identity of $A$, so $n$ is an isomorphism by the affine spectrum--sections correspondence. The normalization isolated-fibre theorem applies because $a$ is separated and finite type. Its isolated-fibre subset is precisely $W$: quasi-finite points are isolated, and conversely an isolated fibre point has the required quasi-finite affine neighbourhoods. Thus its isomorphism $i^{-1}(O)\simeq O$ identifies $W$ with an open of $C$. Composing with $n$ proves that $a|_W$ is an open immersion. The Noetherian-open lemma makes $W$ quasi-compact, hence quasi-affine by its displayed embedding in $\operatorname{Spec}A$. No Noetherianity of $A$ is used.

Apply the qcqs functions localization comparison to $Y\to T$ with multiplicative set $R\setminus\{0\}$. It identifies $A\otimes_R F$ with $\Gamma(Y_F,\mathcal O)$ through the actual pullback of functions. Naturality of the affine adjunction identifies $a_F$ with the canonical map of the affine scheme $Y_F$, so $a_F$ is an isomorphism. For a point $z$ of the generic open of $\operatorname{Spec}A$, the scheme fibre of $a$ over $z$ equals that of $a_F$, hence consists of a single reduced point. The isolated-fibre criterion puts every point of $Y_F$ in $W$. Therefore $W_F=Y_F$, including the empty generic fibre.

source.place: Tag 02KH in degree zero and Schemes 01I1; fibre criterion 01TH.

proof.text: It remains to treat $Y_k\ne\varnothing$. Apply the Dedekind smooth fibre-dense affine lemma with $D=R$ to obtain an affine open $U\subseteq Y$ dense in both fibres. Its stated geometric density implies ordinary density: a nonempty affine open in a fibre remains nonempty after extending its field to an algebraic closure, since its nonzero coordinate vector space stays nonzero on tensoring with a field extension. If the open missed $U$, its base change would contradict geometric density. Smoothness gives flatness, and the flat-DVR Cartier lemma says that multiplication by $\pi$ is injective in each stalk, with special-fibre ideal $(\pi)$. Smooth base change and the smooth-field lemma make $Y_k$ normal and reduced; normal ascent makes $Y$ normal.

source.place: BLR 6.4 Lemma 4 and pp.155--156 construction; Stacks 056T, 034F, 02OO.

proof.text: The Noetherian topology and normal-component theorem decompose $Y$ into finitely many disjoint open integral components. The generic point of any component lies over $F$: otherwise $\pi$ would be zero at that generic stalk, contradicting its being a non-zero-divisor there. Thus $Y_F$ is dense in $Y$. Since $U_F$ is dense in $Y_F$, $U$ is dense in $Y$. The same component theorem applies to the normal Noetherian special fibre $Y_k$, giving generic points of its finitely many components, each belonging to $U_k$.

source.place: Tags 01OZ and 0357; BLR 6.5 Lemma 6, density preparation.

proof.text: Put $Z=|Y|\setminus|U|$. Each generic point $\xi$ of a component of $Z$ has $\dim\mathcal O_{Y,\xi}=1$ by the affine-boundary lemma. Such a $\xi$ cannot lie in $Y_k$. Indeed, a generic point $\zeta$ of a component of $Y_k$ containing $\xi$ generalizes $\xi$, and a generic point $\eta$ of the component of $Y$ containing $\zeta$ generalizes $\zeta$. Here $\eta\ne\zeta$ by step 6. If $\xi\ne\zeta$, this gives a chain of length two, contradicting the stalk-dimension formula. If $\xi=\zeta$, it belongs to $U_k$ by step 6, contradicting $\xi\in Z$. Therefore all generic points of $Z$ lie in $Y_F$. Since $Z$ is a finite union of their closures, $Z=\overline{Z\cap Y_F}$ (closure inside $Y$).

source.place: Tag 0BCV, lemma-complement-affine-open; Tag 02IZ, stalk dimension and generalizations.

proof.text: Choose $x\in Y_k$ and let $Y_i$ be its integral open-and-closed component, with generic point $\eta$. By step 6, $\eta\in U_F$. Since $Y_F$ is affine, its principal-open basis gives $g\in\Gamma(Y_F,\mathcal O)$ with $\eta\in D(g)\subseteq U_F$. The localization comparison of step 4 writes $g=b/r$ with $b\in A$ and $0\ne r\in R$. Thus $D(b)_F=D(g)$. The germ $b_x$ is nonzero: on the integral component $Y_i$, restriction of a section to its generic point and to any other stalk embeds into the same fraction field. Explicitly, on any nonempty affine chart its ring is a domain, and the stalk maps are its prime localizations, so a section zero on a neighbourhood of $x$ would vanish at $\eta$. This contradicts $\eta\in D(b)$.

source.place: BLR 6.5 Lemma 6, choosing the generic principal open; Tags 00E0, 02KH and 01HV.

proof.text: The local ring $B=\mathcal O_{Y,x}$ is Noetherian: take a Noetherian affine chart and localize at the prime of $x$. The ideal $(\pi)B$ lies in its maximal ideal, hence in its Jacobson radical. Krull intersection, with the cyclic finite module $M=B$, gives $\bigcap_n\pi^nB=0$. Since $b_x\ne0$, the set of $n$ for which $b\in\pi^n A$ is bounded and nonempty, and therefore has a largest element $n$. Choose $f\in A$ with $b=\pi^n f$. Then $f\notin\pi A$, while $D(f)_F=D(b)_F\subseteq U_F$ because $\pi$ is invertible over $F$. This proves that division by a maximal power of $\pi$ terminates, rather than assuming $A$ itself Noetherian or $\pi$-adically separated.

source.place: Tag 00IQ, lemma-intersection-powers-ideal-module (2); local rings of a locally Noetherian scheme.

proof.text: The natural map $A/\pi A\to\Gamma(Y_k,\mathcal O)$ is injective. To see this directly, if a section restricts to zero on $Y_k$, its germs belong to the ideal $(\pi)$, so locally it is $\pi h$. The local quotients $h$ agree on overlaps because multiplication by $\pi$ is injective, and the sheaf axiom glues them to a global quotient. Hence the kernel is exactly $\pi A$. Since $f\notin\pi A$, its restriction to $Y_k$ is nonzero. It is nonvanishing at some point of $Y_k$: otherwise on every affine chart it would lie in every prime ideal, hence be nilpotent, and reducedness would force it to be zero. Consequently $(Y_f)_k\ne\varnothing$.

source.place: BLR 6.5 preparation before Lemma 6: reduction modulo the uniformizer; Stacks 02OO and 056T.

proof.text: The closed set $Y\setminus Y_f$ contains $Z\cap Y_F$ since $D(f)_F\subseteq U_F$. By step 7 it therefore contains $Z$, so $Y_f\subseteq U$. Inside the affine $U$, this is exactly the principal open $U_{f|_U}$ and hence is affine. Apply the affine-principal-affinization isomorphism lemma to the qcqs scheme $Y$: it identifies $a:Y_f\to D(f)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A$ with an isomorphism. Every point of $Y_f$ thus has an isolated fibre for $a$, so the isolated-fibre criterion gives $Y_f\subseteq W$. Step 10 proves $W_k\ne\varnothing$. If $Y_k$ is empty there is no special-fibre assertion; if $Y$ is empty all maps and opens above are empty and steps 1--4 already prove the conclusions. The construction makes no componentwise special-fibre density claim.

source.place: BLR 6.5 Lemma 6, closing argument; Stacks Tags 01P8 and 01TH.

Step 3 uses relative normalization (iii) on the whole of Spec A: the integral closure of A in A is A, so n is an isomorphism, and the Zariski Main node gives a|_W as an open immersion. W equals the isolated-fibre set in both directions (quasi-finite-at-point-isolated; affine-pairs matches the pqf-def-quasifinite clause). Step 4 uses the qcqs localization with S=R\{0}, so a_F is an isomorphism and W_F=Y_F. Steps 5-7: the Dedekind dense-affine hypotheses all hold. π is a non-zero-divisor from the Cartier lemma (π=ud, d=vπ ⇒ uv=1), and no generic point lies in Y_k. The boundary lemma with the stalk-dimension chain shows Z is the closure of Z∩Y_F. Steps 8-11: the germ b_x is nonzero on the integral component. Krull intersection is applied in the Noetherian ring O_{Y,x} (not A) and gives a maximal π-power division, so f∉πA. ker(A→Γ(Y_k))=πA, and Y_k is reduced, so (Y_f)_k≠∅. Y_f⊂U, and the principal-affinization isomorphism gives Y_f⊂W. Edge cases checked: Y empty, Y_k empty, Y affine, disconnected Y. Batch-5: lem-trf-smooth-geometrically-normal and lem-trf-normal-topologically-noetherian-components are general scheme facts, not trace-formula or Poincaré content. The Dedekind node reaches sec-trace-formula only through the latter, so all three citations are accepted. The off-unit generic tool_uses are accepted. lean.statement: theorem trait_affine_generic_affinization_locus (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsDiscreteValuationRing R] (Y : Scheme.{u}) (f : Y ⟶ Spec (.of R)) [Smooth f] [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] (hGeneric : IsAffine (pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R (FractionRing R)))))) : IsSeparated Y.toSpecΓ ∧ LocallyOfFiniteType Y.toSpecΓ ∧ QuasiCompact Y.toSpecΓ ∧ ∃ W : Y.Opens, (∀ y : Y, y ∈ W ↔ Y.toSpecΓ.IsQuasiFiniteAtPoint y) ∧ IsCompact (W : Set Y) ∧ (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R (FractionRing R))))) ⁻¹ᵁ W = ⊤ ∧ IsOpenImmersion (W.ι ≫ Y.toSpecΓ) ∧ W.toScheme.IsQuasiAffine ∧ (Nonempty (pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (IsLocalRing.residue R)))) → Nonempty (pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) (W.ι ≫ f) (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (IsLocalRing.residue R)))))
